ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A certain experimental train, following a pre-defined linear motion pattern, employs a computer-controlled braking system to achieve a safe and precise station stop. The braking system consists of two components: electrical braking and mechanical braking. Figure 1 illustrates the variation of the magnitude of the train's acceleration $a_{c}$ with respect to its velocity $v$ during the station stop process.


1. Determine the time $t$ and the distance traveled $x$ required for the train's velocity to decrease from $20\mathrm{m/s}$ to $3\mathrm{m/s}$. (Keep one decimal place).

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A certain experimental train, following a pre-defined linear motion pattern, employs a computer-controlled braking system to achieve a safe and precise station stop. The braking system consists of two components: electrical braking and mechanical braking. Figure 1 illustrates the variation of the magnitude of the train's acceleration $a_c$ with respect to its velocity $v$ during the station stop process. 1. Determine the time $t$ and the distance traveled $x$ required for the train's velocity to decrease from $20\mathrm{m/s}$ to $3\mathrm{m/s}$. (Keep one decimal place).
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure 1 on the left side of the attached figure is a graph of the relationship between acceleration magnitude a and speed v, with the vertical axis labeled a/(m·s^-2) and the horizontal axis labeled v/(m·s^-1). Between v=3 m/s and v=20 m/s, the curve is a horizontal line segment, corresponding to a_c=0.7 m/s^2. Figure 2 on the right side of the figure is a circuit schematic diagram, and is unrelated to the motion calculation in this question of decelerating from 20 m/s to 3 m/s. Reasoning calculation: The problem asks for the time and displacement required for the speed to decrease from 20 m/s to 3 m/s. According to Figure 1, over the entire interval 3–20 m/s, the magnitude of the braking acceleration is constantly 0.7 m/s^2, so it is treated as uniformly decelerated motion. The time t=(20-3)/0.7=17/0.7≈24.3 s. For displacement, use v_f^2=v_i^2-2a x, giving x=(20^2-3^2)/(2×0.7)=391/1.4≈279.3 m.
